audit.why: Ranged mage with two escapes (Across the Veil W, and the hop on The Weirding E). She controls the early walk-up; Aatrox wins once she is out of W.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 phase text was a generic template that named no ultimate and no cooldown.
audit.why: Between Worlds (R) is 140/120/100 and creates a zone that walls the fight off. Your World Ender is 120/100/80 — cheaper, so you can spend it more freely once you are inside her zone.
audit.corrected: Between Worlds (R) walls the fight off on a 140s cooldown — step out before it closes. World Ender out-drains her chip once Across the Veil (W, 22s at rank 1) is spent.

audit.whatIsWrong: Key Ability Interactions described Infernal Chains (W) as a root; Riot’s text says enemies are dragged back to the centre if they do not leave the zone, and the decisive interaction for this matchup was absent.
audit.why: Spirit Abjuration (P) heals her off every spell she lands, so Grievous Wounds timing decides extended trades. Across the Veil (W, 22/21/20/19/18) is her only real escape — that cooldown is your kill window.
audit.corrected: Your Q sweetspot (outer edge) is your damage and your heal — land the edge, never the inner hit, and use E mid-cast to swing the sweetspot onto her. Infernal Chains (W) drags her back to the centre if she doesn't leave the zone — hold it for Across the Veil (W, 22s at rank 1) and she has nothing left to leave with. Vs a ranged laner save E to close the gap, not for chip. Spirit Abjuration (P) heals her off every spell landed, so buy Grievous Wounds before you try to win a long fight.

edits.before: Ultimate interaction changes all-ins. At level 6, reassess the matchup. Aatrox gains his ultimate, but Aurora's ultimate or scaling pattern may change whether you can commit.
edits.after: Between Worlds (R) walls the fight off on a 140s cooldown — step out before it closes. World Ender out-drains her chip once Across the Veil (W, 22s at rank 1) is spent.

edits.before: Your Q sweetspot (outer edge) is your damage and your heal — land the edge, never the inner hit, and use E mid-cast to swing the sweetspot onto Aurora. W (Infernal Chains) roots him if he doesn't leave the zone: use it to lock him for Q2/Q3 or to cut off his escape. Vs a ranged laner, save E to close the gap or dodge poke — not for chip damage; you only win once you're on top of him. Pop R (World Ender) for the heal, AD and move speed when you fully commit or to survive Between Worlds — never burn it for a single Q.
